import sys
from collections import defaultdict

# Constants
MOD = 1000000007
INV = 570000004

def add(a, b):
    return a + b if a + b < MOD else a + b - MOD

def sub(a, b):
    return a - b + MOD if a < b else a - b

def mul(a, b):
    return (a * b) % MOD

n = int(sys.stdin.readline())

# Using a dictionary to simulate unordered_map with bitset keys
name = {}
dfn = 0
# son will be a list of lists, size depends on number of nodes
# Since number of nodes is unknown initially, we will initialize as needed
son = []

def dfs(s):
    global dfn
    if s in name:
        return name[s]
    ret = dfn
    name[s] = ret
    # Ensure son list is large enough
    while len(son) <= ret:
        son.append([0] * (1 << n))
    for i in range(1 << n):
        t = s
        for j in range(1 << n):
            if not t[j]:
                k_mask = i & j
                k = k_mask
                while k:
                    lsb = k & -k
                    if s[j ^ lsb]:
                        t[j] = 1
                        break
                    k ^= lsb
        son[ret][i] = dfs(t)
    dfn += 1
    return ret

# Read matrix p
p = []
for _ in range(n):
    row = list(map(int, sys.stdin.readline().split()))
    p.append([mul(val, INV) for val in row])

# Precompute q
q = []
for i in range(n):
    q_row = []
    for j in range(1 << n):
        val = 1
        for k in range(n):
            if (j >> k) & 1:
                val = mul(val, p[k][i])
            else:
                val = mul(val, sub(1, p[k][i]))
        q_row.append(val)
    q.append(q_row)

# Initialize DP array
dp = [[0] * (1 << n) for _ in range(n + 1)]
dp[0][0] = 1

# Run DFS to build the tree
dfs(1)

# Compute the result
res_bitset = 1
res = [0] * (1 << n)
res[0] = 1
for i in range(1 << n):
    res[i] = 1
res_node = dfs(res)

for i in range(n):
    for j in range(dfn):
        for k in range(1 << n):
            dp[i + 1][son[j][k]] = add(dp[i + 1][son[j][k]], mul(dp[i][j], q[i][k]))

print(dp[n][res_node])
